cards.speaker: mirren
cards.text: The study drawer. The one that's locked. Did you try it? He kept the tide tables there. And other things.

left.label: I forced it
left.outcome: "Right." She goes white and does not leave.

right.label: I was waiting for you
right.outcome: She has the key. She has had it the whole time.

cards.speaker: mirren
cards.text: Tide tables, on a canal. Pages of figures in his hand that aren't figures. He was writing something so nobody would read it. Nobody has.

right.label: Let me take it
right.outcome: "You can look. It stays in the house."

cards.speaker: src_ledger
cards.text: Dray's ledger, open on the desk at night. The columns run the wrong way for money. Every page begins with the same nine marks, then changes.

left.label: Copy the nine marks
left.outcome: Nine. Like the locks. Like the reservoirs.

right.label: Sleep; it will keep
right.outcome: It has kept a year already.

cards.speaker: fennick
cards.text: You'll never guess. In strictest confidence: Dray asked me once what the wire code was for numbers. Not letters. Numbers. I shouldn't have told him. I did.

left.label: Tell me too
left.outcome: He does, in a whisper, in the telegraph office, with the door open.

right.label: Ask what else he asked
right.outcome: "Where the wire goes at night. I said Ardent. He said no, where does it go."

cards.speaker: mirren
cards.text: It's a cipher. It has to be. He taught me one when I was small, a game with the gauge marks. I thought it was a game.

left.label: Teach it to me
left.outcome: She draws the sill on the table in spilled ale.

right.label: Work it yourself; I'll keep the gate
right.outcome: She works it. She does not come to the paddles for two days.

cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: You have been in the study at night. The lamp is visible from the Company house. For the record, the late Keeper's papers are Company property. You will find I would like them.

left.label: There are no papers
left.outcome: "Noted." She writes it down, which is worse.

right.label: Tide tables; take them
right.outcome: You give her the tide tables. Not the other pages.

cards.speaker: tobin
cards.text: Dray? Course I knew Dray. In my day the gauge had nine marks and a tenth nobody used, painted over. He asked me about the tenth. Nobody asks about the tenth.

left.label: Ask about the tenth
left.outcome: "Below the sill. For when the pound went dry. It did, once."

right.label: Buy him another and wait
right.outcome: He talks about weather for an hour, and then about the tenth mark anyway.

cards.speaker: mirren
cards.text: Ten marks, not nine. That's the key. Every page is a day and every number is a place on the gauge. It isn't a diary. It's a map of something.

left.label: A map of the pound
left.outcome: "No. The numbers go below the sill. Under."

right.label: A map of somewhere under
right.outcome: She looks at you a long time. "He went under something."

cards.speaker: src_ledger
cards.text: Past midnight, the cipher gives up its last page. Three letters, twice. S.H. And a bearing from the top gate along the north bank.

left.label: Sluice house
left.outcome: You have walked past it forty times.

right.label: Someone's initials
right.outcome: Nobody at the summit has them. The building does.

cards.speaker: fennick
cards.text: I kept a copy. Of his last wire. I keep copies of everything, I shouldn't, I know. 'FOUND THE KEY STOP GOING TO SEE STOP IF NOT BACK TELL M STOP.' He never sent the second one.

left.label: Give me the copy
left.outcome: He does. His hand shakes; yours doesn't, yet.

right.label: Give it to Mirren
right.outcome: "Tell M." He understands, and goes red.

cards.speaker: vosk
cards.text: The telegraph clerk has been indiscreet. For the record, the late Keeper resigned. His wire is a Company document. You have a copy. I would like it.

left.label: Hand it over
left.outcome: "Noted. You will find this was wise."

cards.speaker: mirren
cards.text: 'Tell M.' He didn't come back and nobody told me. Nobody told me anything. You know where he went now. Are you going to tell me, or are you going to be like them?

left.label: The sluice house
left.outcome: She nods. She has known, or guessed, or feared.

right.label: Not until I've seen it
right.outcome: "That's what he'd have said." It is not a compliment.

cards.speaker: mirren
cards.text: In the oilskin. The one on the hook. Inside pocket, sewn shut. I never looked. Look.

left.label: Open the seam
left.outcome: A brass key, stamped S.H. Cold as the pound.

right.label: You open it
right.outcome: She does. She holds the key a long time before she gives it to you.

cards.speaker: src_ledger
cards.text: The key is heavy for its size. Vosk would like it. Mirren wants it. The sluice house door has waited a year and does not mind waiting another night.

left.label: Keep it; go alone, soon
left.outcome: You put it on the ring beside the gate keys.

right.label: Give it to Vosk
right.outcome: "Noted." She does not ask where you found it. She knows.

cards.speaker: mirren
cards.text: You gave it to her. His key. To her. Get out of his chair.

left.label: It was Company property
left.outcome: She leaves the oilskin on the hook and does not come back for a week.

cards.notes: Reached via delayed follow-up from ma02_14 right; forced pool so it never appears otherwise.
